islands.law:
# The atlas's value wave, as a law of nature. Transcribed from Atlas._wave:
#
#     V = max(source, best neighbour * (1 - decay)^distance) * passable
#
# with decay 0.06 (0.94 per orthogonal step, 0.94^sqrt2 = 0.916214 per diagonal)
# and a solid cell letting `leak` of the wave through — the harness's per-cell
# leak, innate then taught per hue by what pressing on it did.
# max8 also contains the four orthogonal neighbours, but they are discounted
# more there than under max4, so the max of the two is exactly the eight-way
# wave with a diagonal that costs sqrt 2. The harness paints source and solid
# each thought, steps this `subticks` times, and reads value at the centre.

channel source
channel solid
channel value

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(source, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Confinement suppression (night lab 2026-09-23, champion #35): a source hemmed in by
# solid counts less, so local food in a nook stops dominating and the frontier wins there.
# 24.5 meals on 32 never-seen FINAL worlds vs 18.8 the reference wave, 17.1 the tuned ghost.

channel source
channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel here
channel value
channel confinement
channel injection

# Measure local solidity to detect dead-ends/corridors.
# High sum8(solid) means tight space.
rule calc_conf:
  when 1
  set confinement = sum8(solid)

# Inject signals, but suppress heavily if in a tight space.
# The division by (1 + k*conf) reduces value in dead-ends.
# This prevents the agent from being pulled into local maxima in confined areas.
rule inject:
  when 1
  set injection = max(thing, source) / (1 + 0.5 * confinement)

# Propagate the value wave.
# Use standard Bellman decay. The suppressed injection ensures dead-ends don't dominate.
rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(injection, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Sources linger: a commitment law. The smell of a thing behind a wall is
# painted where the world's geodesic bearing points, and that bearing flips
# between the two ways round as the agent takes a step each way (seen on world
# 7: eleven frames out of twelve on the same spot, the source hopping left and
# right of it). Here a painted source keeps ~94% of itself per thought after
# the paint moves on, so the wave still holds the place it was first told and
# the nearer of the two stays the target. Where the agent stands there is
# nothing: `here` and its ring erase the ghost (an eaten morsel leaves no
# ghost to circle).

channel source
channel solid
channel here
channel value
channel ghost: init 0

rule linger:
  when 1
  set ghost = max(source, 0.99 * ghost) * (1 - here) * (1 - max8(here))

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(ghost, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Target lock: the decision's whole PATH (gradient climb from the agent) is traced every
# step; the source it ends on accumulates LOCK, and lock makes that source brighter.

channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel here
channel bad
channel leak
channel value
channel trail
channel confinement
channel thr

channel probe

# Trail of visited cells (centre + a faint ring), slow fade, bounded in [0, 1].

  when 1

  set confinement = sum8(solid)

# On the path: the value a neighbour must reach to be this cell's next step (uphill only).
rule calc_thr:
  when 1
  set thr = where(chain > 0, max(max8(value) - 0.00001, value + 0.00001 - 9 * here), 9)

  when 1

observations.text: The agent is born in a sealed slot about two cells wide and seven tall, between two rock masses in the middle of the map, and it never leaves it: the whole track, cyan through red, is a short up-and-down shuttle inside that slot, and it starves a cell below where it started. It is not idle. It hits the rock 22 times and the brown chipped cells show it working on two different faces, the cap above the slot and the wall to its upper right, but neither gives way, so it never makes a door and never sees any of the food growing in the open ground just above and to the left. The failing is that it doesn't stick with one face: its own trail covers every cell of so small a room, and the probe term is cut by that trail, so all the wall faces fade together. None of them stays brighter than the rest, so the wave sends the agent back and forth between the top and the side and it chips a little at each. The fix I would make first is commitment to a face: a wall cell that has already given (chipped) should become a stronger source that does not fade, exempt from the trail spending, so the agent keeps striking the same spot until it breaks through instead of spreading its blows over every wall of

The agent makes one long, purposeful migration from its start in the top-right corner diagonally down to the bottom-left, eating steadily along a narrow corridor of the map, with one tight curl in the centre where it circles a few times before moving on. Late in life (the red part) it stops travelling and wanders tangled back and forth inside one small patch near the bottom-left. It eats only a little there while the whole left half, the top and the right side, all full of growing food, are never visited.
